instruction:
# Write a Funny Runme Poem

Write a short, funny poem about Runme, notebooks, terminals, or developer
workflow.

Save the poem at:

```text
poem.txt
```

The verifier will judge the poem's humor with an LLM.

blocks.body:
name = "runmedev/poem-judge"
description = "Poem-writing task graded by an LLM-as-a-judge verifier."
authors = []
keywords = ["runme", "harbor", "containerless", "llm", "judge"]

[about]
difficulty = "easy"
category = "behavior"
tags = ["runme", "harbor", "llm-as-a-judge", "verifier-env"]

[agent]
timeout = "8m"

[sandbox]
cpus = 1
memory = "1 GB"
disk = "1 GB"
gpus = 0
workdir = "/app/examples/harbor/datasets/runme-llm-judge/poem-judge/workdir"
env = {}
build_timeout = "1m"

[verifier]
timeout = "15m"
mount = "/tests"

# From verifier/judge.toml by tools/convert.py --convert-judges. RewardKit 0.1.7, the newest release ~=0.1.0 admits: its defaults for effort, per, timeout are written out.
[verifier.judges.llm]
model = "openai/gpt-5.6-terra"
effort = "medium"
per = "rubric"
samples = 1
timeout = "5m"

[oracle]
env = {}
mount = "/solution"

[import.harbor]
schema_version = "1.1"

[import.harbor.rewardkit]
installs = "harbor-rewardkit~=0.1.0"
scripts = ["verifier/test.sh"]
judges = []
converted = ["verifier/judge.toml"]
defaults = "0.1.7"
env = { OPENAI_API_KEY = "${OPENAI_API_KEY}" }

[import.harbor.rewardkit.kept]
"tests/test.sh" = "sha256:1b4dd117dea44035c94f247ce62ad670dd8692d12340ea0a61f92280a7d1ca52"

config.name: runmedev/poem-judge
config.description: Poem-writing task graded by an LLM-as-a-judge verifier.

criteria.text: Rate how funny the poem is. Consider whether it has a clear joke, surprise, wordplay, or a playful take on developer workflow.

diagnostics.message: import.harbor.rewardkit.env.OPENAI_API_KEY resolves ${OPENAI_API_KEY} from the host; a runtime resolves it only if the operator allows that variable, and never a provider key: a seat that calls a model gets the runtime's proxy and a scoped token instead
'funny' does not say where the agent is told about it: quote the instruction in stated, or explain in implicit why the agent should know
